constructions.title: Admissible windows of consecutive years
constructions.what: How many windows of consecutive whole years, each at least a minimum length, fit inside an index period.
constructions.model: With $n$ years in the period and a minimum length $w$, a window is fixed by its first and last year, and windows of length $L$ number $n - L + 1$, so the total is $\sum_{L=w}^{n}(n-L+1) = \dfrac{(n-w+1)(n-w+2)}{2}$, in the code `(nyears - wmin + 1) * (nyears - wmin + 2) // 2`, with `nyears` computed as `last - first + 1` from the stated first and last year.
assumptions: A window is a run of consecutive years with both ends inside the index period; windows of every length from the minimum to the whole period count, each once.

justified.text: The closed form is the sum of an arithmetic series; the generator refuses the page if it differs from the enumeration over every window length.

gaps: Whether every window holds enough stations in each year for a fit is not checked: the count is of windows, not of fits.
void_if: the test admits windows that skip years
a window must also hold a minimum number of stations each year
constructions.licenses: The number of windows the slope surface of the L3 test is computed over.
constructions.not_licensed: Anything about the slopes fitted in them.
